title: A Ledger for the Orchard
premise: In 1848, on the eve of revolution in a river city under imperial watch, Dominic Hartwell has survived seven years in her father's print shop by mastering the silences that keep people safe. When a stranger arrives bearing letters in the unmistakable hand of Tomas Veyra — her father's old apprentice, officially dead for three years — she discovers the 'corpse' is alive, exiled, and the sole witness to a massacre the governor's ledger was forged to erase. Dominic must smuggle the true ledger past three checkpoints and downriver before the ice breaks, choosing between loyalty to the shop that raised her and the truth that could free or destroy them all. She delivers the ledger at terrible cost: her father dies covering her escape, the truth ignites the uprising, and Dominic, no longer silent, becomes the voice that prints it.
about_author: Gideon Delacroix is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print shops across Central Europe before turning to fiction. He writes historical novels about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Letters
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Establishes the print shop, her father Aldous's failing eyesight, and the unspoken rules of survival under the governor's censors. She sets type for an official proclamation she knows contains lies. Emotional beat: weary competence masking suppressed anger.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Loading Door
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On a frozen night, a wounded stranger named Ilan begs entry, carrying sealed letters in the handwriting of Tomas Veyra — dead three years by official record. Aldous goes pale and lets him in anyway. Emotional beat: shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: What the Corpse Wrote
chapters.summary: Alternating flashbacks through Aldous's POV. We learn Tomas was Aldous's brilliant apprentice who fled after discovering the governor's forged massacre ledger. The letters claim Tomas lives in exile and holds proof. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a drowned body.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One River
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. He explains the plan: the true ledger must reach the printers' guild in Velmora before the ice breaks, passing the customs house, the garrison bridge, and the governor's private wharf. Emotional beat: desperate urgency meeting practical impossibility.

chapters.title: The Governor's Compliment
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Captain Reiner of the garrison visits the shop, praising their loyalty while noting the new press restrictions — a veiled threat. He lingers over Dominic's hands, ink-stained like a man's. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Lessons in Disappearing
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. He teaches Dominic the old tricks: hidden compartments in type cases, messages set in pi fonts, water-soluble inks. For the first time he treats her as a cutter, not a daughter. Emotional beat: bittersweet inheritance.

chapters.title: The Widow Veyra
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She visits Tomas's widow Marta, who believes her husband dead and hates the Hartwells for it. Dominic leaves without telling her the truth — the first lie that costs her. Emotional beat: shame over necessary cruelty.

chapters.title: Ice Under Pressure
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. A spy in the resistance network is suspected; Ilan suspects everyone, including the Hartwells. He tests Dominic with false information and catches her hesitation. Emotional beat: brittle trust negotiated between strangers.

chapters.title: The Ledger Described
chapters.summary: Tomas's letters, read aloud. The ledger records not just the massacre but payments to every official who signed the forgery — names that reach into the garrison itself. Emotional beat: revelation transforming fear into purpose.

chapters.title: Reiner's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Reiner returns with a warrant to search the shop, ostensibly for seditious type. Aldous's hidden compartment nearly betrays them; Dominic improvises, sacrificing her own secret engravings to satisfy him. Emotional beat: terror mastered through quick thinking.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Guild Hall
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. The resistance contact at the printers' guild turns out to be the informer; two couriers are taken. Ilan escapes but realizes the original route is burned. Emotional beat: despair narrowing options to one suicidal path.

chapters.title: Father and Daughter, Cutting Type
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Father and daughter work through the night cutting a duplicate title page and forging travel passes. Aldous confesses his role in Tomas's flight — he chose silence seven years ago to protect the shop. Emotional beat: reconciliation through shared craft.

chapters.title: Marta Learns the Truth
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic tells Marta that Tomas lives, and Marta's fury at the years of mourning nearly undoes everything — until she offers her late husband's riverboat papers. Emotional beat: forgiveness earned at the price of honesty.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, disguised as a widow shipping funeral goods downriver, the ledger sewn into a shroud lining. A clerk with a suspicious eye demands she unwrap the shroud. Emotional beat: ice-cold nerve holding under scrutiny.

chapters.title: The Informer's Face
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. Ilan identifies the informer — young Petrik, whose brother died in the massacre and who sold out for protection. Instead of killing him, they show him the ledger's pages naming his brother among the dead. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into allegiance.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Garrison Bridge
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Reiner himself inspects traffic on the bridge, hunting the courier. Petrik creates a diversion that goes wrong; Ilan is captured buying time for Dominic to cross. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt in motion.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV under torture. He gives up nothing, but Reiner deduces the ledger is already moving and locks down the river. Emotional beat: endurance as quiet heroism.

chapters.title: The Shop Burns
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Retaliating soldiers torch the print shop. Aldous stays behind to feed the fire with the incriminating archives so nothing implicates Dominic, and does not come out. Emotional beat: sacrifice as final act of authorship.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Governor's Wharf
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, grieving and hunted. The only way onto a boat is through the governor's private wharf — and she walks in wearing her father's coat, posing as his clerk delivering a last consignment. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into audacity.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Aboard the boat as the river groans and cracks, Reiner boards for a final inspection. Petrik, now loyal, vouches for her; the ice breaks and the boat slips free as Reiner realizes too late. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: The Reading in Velmora
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In Velmora, the guild prints ten thousand copies of the ledger overnight. The names are read aloud in the square; the crowd that gathers becomes the revolution. Ilan, freed in the chaos, finds her amid the presses. Emotional beat: catharsis — silence broken at last.

chapters.title: A New Face for Old Words
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue. Months later, she cuts a new typeface in a rebuilt shop — her own design, named for her father — and takes on an apprentice of her own, teaching not silence but voice. Marta receives the first printed copy. Emotional beat: belonging found in craft and truth.
